issues.evidence: FE1.1 BUS_B (pin 36) pulled to 5V by R10 100k. Per the FE1.1 datasheet, BUS_B is 'bus power indicator, active low'. Driving it high tells the host the hub is self-powered. In practice the only fitted supply is the upstream USB-C VBUS (J5 A4/A9/B4/B9), and the optional external header J6 is DNP. VBUSM (R11/R29) senses that same 5V net.
issues.why_it_matters: The host will not budget power: each downstream port is advertised as 500 mA while the hub actually runs off a single upstream port with 5k1 Rd only (default USB power). Heavy downstream loads can brown out the hub or trip the host port.

issues.evidence: J6 (2-pin header, DNP) ties directly onto net 5V. That net is the upstream USB-C VBUS (J5 VBUS pins) and also feeds VBUSM. There is no diode, ideal-diode or switch in between.
issues.why_it_matters: If J6 is ever fitted and used as an external 5V input, it back-drives the host's VBUS (forbidden by the USB spec, and it can damage the host or the PSU). VBUSM also stays high with no host attached, so attach detection breaks.
issues.time_or_money: only matters if J6 is populated

issues.evidence: The AP22652A ILIM resistors are 12k. The datasheet gives about 1.7 A at 15k, so 12k is roughly 2.1 A per port, about 8 A total across 4 ports. All of it comes from one upstream USB-C VBUS with no input fuse or upstream current limit.
issues.why_it_matters: The per-port limits do not protect the upstream source. A few charging loads can exceed what the host port can supply.
issues.time_or_money: design choice; consider lower ILIM or external supply

acceptable_designs.reason: Each CC pin has its own 5k1 Rd to GND (R5, R6). This is the correct UFP sink termination.

In the local symbol, FE1.1 OVCB pins are typed output. The datasheet defines them as inputs (active-low over-current indicators). They are driven by the open-drain AP22652 FAULT pins, so the output-to-output ERC conflict is only a symbol pin-type artefact.
These pull-ups go to 5V although FE1.1 runs on a 3.3V core. The FE1.1 datasheet gives VIH max 5.5V for its digital inputs, so the inputs are 5V tolerant.
These are port-indicator LED pairs between LEDn and DRV, wired as in FE1.1 Fig. 5. Every LED has a series resistor (510R or 12k), and D9 is the optional hub-active LED on DRV via R7.
The 12k LED resistors (about 0.25 mA) are a deliberate choice for dim indicators, not an error.

USBLC6-2SC6 is used in flow-through mode: pins 1/6 and 3/4 are the same I/O line internally. Each data line therefore gets two net names, one connector-side and one hub-side. This is ST's recommended layout, so it is not a broken pair.
DIS_REG (pin 37) and TEST (pin 40) are tied to GND as the datasheet requires: internal 5V-to-3.3V regulator enabled, normal mode.

Each downstream VBUS sits behind an AP22652A current-limited switch with a FAULT line back to the hub. The upstream side relies on the host port's own protection, which is normal for a bus-powered hub.
4-layer board: all USB pairs run on F.Cu, length-matched within 0.01 mm, with no vias, over a solid GND pour on In1.Cu/In2.Cu (100% coverage by point sampling).
Y1 (LCSC C50430, X322512MMB4SI) has CL = 10 pF. With 12 pF per side plus a few pF of stray, the effective load is about 9-11 pF, which is correct.
2K7 1% to ground matches the FE1.1 requirement.

[acceptable] All 14 LEDs carry LCSC codes (C965812, C965819, C2297) that fully identify each part; value 'LED' with an LCSC field is normal JLC practice. Only a BOM grouped on value+footprint alone would merge the colours.

notes: FE1.1 pin mapping in lib:FE1.1 verified against FE1.1 datasheet Rev 1.11 (all 48 pins match). VREG18 and VD33_OUT each have the required 10uF (C26, C25), and 3V3/1V8 decoupling sits 1-6 mm from the pins. USBLC6 orientation (pins 1/6, 3/4) checked. AP22652A pinout (IN1 GND2 EN3 FAULT4 ILIM5 OUT6) and active-low EN checked against search results only, not the full PDF. Not checked: exact AP22652A ILIM formula; USB-A footprint mirror orientation against the SHOU HAN drawing (pad pitch 2.5/2.0/2.5 is consistent); trace impedance (stackup not given). The design looks clean overall; no high-confidence defects found.
